lines.japanese:
「…それでお前、
今年、雪菜ちゃんと何度会ったんだ？」
lines.english: “…So how many times have you seen Setsuna this year?”

lines.japanese: 「…いや、まだ一度も」
lines.english: “…Not once.”

lines.japanese: 「かぁ～、いつまで引きずってんだよ馬鹿！」
lines.english: “God, how long are you going to stay hung up on this, you idiot?”

lines.japanese: 「俺が馬鹿なんて事はわかってんだよ馬鹿！」
lines.english: “I already know I’m an idiot, idiot!”

lines.japanese:
人間、明らかに自分が悪いことをしたと指摘されると、
ついつい普段以上に声を荒げてしまうもので。
lines.english: Tell someone they’re clearly in the wrong, and they’ll tend to raise their voice even louder than usual.

lines.japanese:
久々の武也からの電話に応えていた俺の声は、
そんな感じで嫌なボルテージが上がっていた。
lines.english: That was why my own voice grew nastier by the second as I took Takeya’s first call in ages.

lines.japanese:
「もう二か月以上も会ってないってことだろそれ。
なにグダグダしてんだよ？」
lines.english: “You haven’t seen her in over two months. What the hell are you doing?”

lines.japanese:
「仕方ないだろ！
俺、振られたんだから！
…自分から会おうなんて言える訳ないだろ」
lines.english: “What else can I do? She dumped me! I can’t very well ask to see her myself.”

lines.japanese:
冬休みが空けた頃、
雪菜から、メールが届いた。
lines.english: Around the time winter break ended, I got an email from Setsuna.

lines.japanese:
サブジェクトには『あけましておめでとう』って、
とても友達ライクな言葉が乗っかってた。
lines.english: The subject read “Happy New Year”—the sort of perfectly friendly message one friend might send another.

lines.japanese:
けど中身は、あまり友達っぽくなかった。
それどころか、後悔と逡巡を重ねながらも、
一度突き放したはずの俺に、踏み込んできてた。
lines.english: But the message itself didn’t sound much like a friend. For all its regret and hesitation, she was stepping toward me—the very person she had once pushed away.

lines.japanese:
それからも、お互いのメール交換は頻繁に続き、
俺たちは、互いが一度は別れたんだってことを、
必死に覆い隠すみたいに、優しい会話を続けた。
lines.english: We kept exchanging emails after that, carrying on one gentle conversation after another as though desperately trying to hide the fact that we had once broken up.

lines.japanese: …あれ以来、一度も約束をしないままに。
lines.english: And through it all, neither of us once suggested meeting.

lines.japanese:
「さすがに見守るって言っても限度があるぞ。
大体、お前らがそろってスキー旅行の返事をしないのは、
そのせいだろう？」
lines.english: “There are limits to how long we can stand back and watch. This is why neither of you will answer us about the ski trip, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese:
「だからあれはほら、
日程も何も決まってないから…」
lines.english: “That’s only because you haven’t settled on any dates or anything…”

lines.japanese:
そんな中途半端な俺たちに業を煮やしたのか、
武也と依緒がスキー旅行の誘いをかけてきたのは、
期末試験の終わった二週間前だった。
lines.english: Apparently fed up with the limbo we had put ourselves in, Takeya and Io had invited us on a ski trip two weeks ago, after finals ended.

lines.japanese:
「お前らの空いてる日に合わせるって言ったろ？
それについての返事はどうした？」
lines.english: “We said we’d work around the days you were free. Where’s your answer to that?”

lines.japanese: 「それは…」
lines.english: “Well…”

lines.japanese:
「いつならＯＫなんだよ？
もうすぐ３月だぞ？」
lines.english: “When can you go? It’s almost March.”
“March…”

lines.japanese:
「そろそろ決めてくれよ、春希。
早くしないと雪が溶けちまう」
lines.english: “Decide soon, Haruki. If you wait much longer, the snow will melt.”

lines.japanese: 「武也…」
lines.english: “Takeya…”

lines.japanese:
もうすぐ、冬が終わる。
『ＷＨＩＴＥ　ＡＬＢＵＭの季節』が。
lines.english: Winter would soon be over. The season of White Album.

lines.japanese: 「で、いつならいいんだ？」
lines.english: “So when works for you?”

lines.japanese:
「とりあえず、検討する。
決まったらまた連絡するから」
lines.english: “I’ll think about it and call you when I’ve decided.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、連絡くれるのはいつだ？」
lines.english: “When will that call be?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと…近いうちには」
lines.english: “Uh… soon.”

lines.japanese:
いつも、この季節の移り変わりに、
俺は何かを期待し、そして何かを恐れて過ごす。
lines.english: Every year, as this season began to turn, I waited for something—and feared something else.

lines.japanese:
だって、俺たちの関係が動くのは、
いつもこの季節だったから。
lines.english: Because this was always the season when things between us began to move.

lines.japanese: 「今週中？　明日？　それとも一時間後？」
lines.english: “This week? Tomorrow? An hour from now?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと…鋭意努力する」
lines.english: “Uh… I’ll apply myself with all due urgency.”

lines.japanese:
雪の降る日に俺たちは近づき、
雪の降る夜に俺たちは傷つき。
lines.english: On days when snow fell, we drew closer. On nights when snow fell, we hurt each other.

lines.japanese:
寒さに震えながら抱きあって、
心まで凍えながらすれ違う。
lines.english: We held each other while our bodies shivered, then passed each other by as our hearts froze.

lines.japanese:
今動かなければ、何も起こりはしない。
けれど何か起こってしまったとき、
二人が笑いあえているか、自信がない。
lines.english: If I did nothing, nothing would happen. But if something did, I had no confidence we would still be smiling together afterward.

lines.japanese: 「そっか…」
lines.english: “I see…”

lines.japanese: 「悪いな、武也」
lines.english: “Sorry, Takeya.”

lines.japanese: だから今年の冬も、俺は…
lines.english: So this winter too, I would…

lines.japanese:
「いいよもう…
お前の自主性に任せてたら、
いつまで経っても日程が決まらないことはわかった」
lines.english: “Forget it. I’ve realized that if we wait for you to take the initiative, we’ll never pick a date.”

lines.japanese:
「…あ、悪い。
来客だ」
lines.english: “…Sorry, someone’s at the door.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ、今日はそろそろ切るな。
また連絡するわ」
lines.english: “Then I’ll let you go. I’ll call again.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、またな」
lines.english: “All right. Talk to you later.”

lines.japanese:
俺は、もう一度心の中で武也に詫びると、
通話を切り、そして…
lines.english: I apologized to Takeya once more in my head, ended the call, and then…

lines.japanese: 「どなたです…」
lines.english: “Who is it…?”

lines.japanese: 「よっ」
lines.english: “Yo.”

lines.japanese: 玄関を開けた瞬間…
lines.english: The moment I opened the door…

lines.japanese:
目の前のあまりにもあまりな来客に、
一瞬、言葉を失った。
lines.english: For one speechless moment, I could only stare at the last person I’d expected to find on my doorstep.

lines.japanese:
「という訳だから、
こっちで勝手に日を決めさせてもらった。
今から出発だ、すぐ仕度しろ」
lines.english: “So that settles it. We picked the date ourselves. We leave now, so get packed.”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
「まさか断るなんて言わないよな？
お前は今こうして用事もなく家にいるし、
そして俺たちは既に明日の宿を取ってある」
lines.english: “You’re not going to refuse, are you? You’re home with no plans, and we’ve already reserved rooms for tomorrow night.”
“…Takeya?”

lines.japanese:
「今ごろは依緒も雪菜ちゃんを確保してる頃だ。
さ、すぐに荷物をまとめろ」
lines.english: “Io should have Setsuna secured by now. Come on, pack your things.”

lines.japanese: 今年の冬も、俺は…
lines.english: This winter too, I would…

lines.japanese:
「っ…
ご、ごめんね春希くん」
lines.english: “I-I’m sorry, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「な、何が？」
lines.english: “F-For what?”

lines.japanese: 「何がって、その…」
lines.english: “For… well…”

lines.japanese:
「雪菜が謝ることなんて何もないだろ？
どっちも被害者なんだし…」
lines.english: “You have nothing to apologize for. We’re both victims here.”

lines.japanese:
「で、でも…
春希くん、困ってるんじゃないかって思って」
lines.english: “B-But I thought this might be difficult for you.”

lines.japanese:
「困ってるって言うか、戸惑ってるけど…
で、でもそれなら雪菜だって…」
lines.english: “I wouldn’t say it’s difficult. I’m more… confused. B-But you must be too…”

lines.japanese:
「わ、わたしは、えっと、その。
…確かに、春希くんと同じ感じかも」
lines.english: “I-I’m… well… probably in the same boat.”

lines.japanese: 「だ、だよなぁ」
lines.english: “R-Right.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “Y-Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「今の会話、いかがですか解説の水沢さん」
lines.english: “Your analysis of that exchange, Ms. Mizusawa?”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、あまりにも初々しすぎて、
こっちが恥ずかしくなってきますねぇ。
お前ら知り合って何年だよと突っ込んでやりたいです」
lines.english: “They’re so painfully bashful that I’m embarrassed for them. I’d like to ask how many years they’ve known each other.”

lines.japanese:
「まるで合コン初心者同士の二人が
いつの間にかツーショットになっていたような展開に、
車内騒然としております」
lines.english: “The car is in an uproar at this development: two first-timers at a singles mixer somehow finding themselves alone together.”
“Ngh…”

lines.japanese: 「誰のせいだ誰の！」
lines.english: “Whose fault do you think that is?”

lines.japanese:
「もうすぐ高速だから、
その前にどっかで遅めの晩飯にしようぜ」
lines.english: “We’ll hit the expressway soon. Let’s stop for a late dinner first.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あたし中華がいいな。
この辺で深夜営業やってるところあったっけ」
lines.english: “I-I’d like Chinese. Is anywhere around here open this late?”

lines.japanese:
運転席と助手席に怨嗟の声を投げかけるも、
そこに座ってる連中はあっさりと受け流しやがった。
lines.english: I aimed a resentful groan at the two in the front seats, but they brushed it off.

lines.japanese:
この車に押し込められて１時間…
とっくに日付も変わり、２月の最終日に入った今も、
俺たちは、このありえない急展開についていけてない。
lines.english: We had been trapped in this car for an hour. Midnight had passed, bringing us into the final day of February, and we still couldn’t keep pace with this impossible turn of events.

lines.japanese:
武也に急かされるまま強制的に旅の仕度をさせられ、
そこから強引に車に押し込まれ、
そして見慣れた道をしばらく走ったら…
lines.english: Takeya had rushed me through packing for the trip, shoved me into the car, and driven for a while down familiar roads…

lines.japanese: 「…にしても、よく雪菜の家族を説得できたな、依緒」
lines.english: “…Still, I’m impressed you convinced Setsuna’s family.”

lines.japanese:
小木曽家の前で、
俺と同じように急ごしらえの旅行鞄を持った雪菜が、
依緒にしっかり拘束されていた。
lines.english: Outside the Ogiso home, Io had Setsuna firmly in custody. Like me, she had a hastily packed travel bag.

lines.japanese:
「事前にスキーに行くって話だけはしておいたからね。
その点にぬかりはないよ」
lines.english: “I’d already told them we were planning a ski trip. I had that much covered.”

lines.japanese:
「そうだとしてもいきなり今日なんて…
ご両親怒ったろ？」
lines.english: “Even so, leaving without warning tonight must have made her parents furious.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、それが…」
lines.english: “A-Actually…”

lines.japanese:
「出発日を雪菜がすっかり忘れてたって設定にしたら、
お母さんにやたらと謝られて恐縮したなぁ…」
lines.english: “I told them Setsuna had completely forgotten the departure date. Her mother apologized so profusely that I didn’t know what to do with myself.”

lines.japanese:
「小木曽家全員騙してるじゃないかそれ！
恐縮以前に良心の呵責に苛まれろよ！」
lines.english: “You deceived the entire Ogiso family! Never mind feeling awkward—try feeling guilty!”

lines.japanese:
なんて奴らだ…
目的のためなら友人の家族不和も厭わないのか。
lines.english: What kind of people were these? Would they risk sowing discord in a friend’s family just to get what they wanted?

lines.japanese:
「雪菜、本当にいいのかよそんなんで？
雪菜が家族に嘘をつくなんて、今まで…」
lines.english: “Setsuna, are you really all right with this? You’ve never lied to your family before…”

lines.japanese: 今まで…？
lines.english: Never?

lines.japanese:
「仕方ないよ…
もう宿予約しちゃったって言うし。
もし断ったら、今度は二人に悪いよ」
lines.english: “I couldn’t help it. They said the rooms were already booked. Refusing now would be unfair to them.”

lines.japanese:
「こいつらに申し訳なく思う必要なんかないだろ。
こっちの承諾もなしに勝手に突っ走りやがって…」
lines.english: “You don’t owe these two anything. They charged ahead without asking either of us.”

lines.japanese: 「水沢さんいかがですか今の発言は？」
lines.english: “Ms. Mizusawa, your thoughts on that statement?”

lines.japanese:
「ん～、どこにでも空気を読まない輩と言うのは
いるものですね～」
lines.english: “Some people just can’t read the room.”

lines.japanese: 「だからお前らちょっと黙ってろっての！」
lines.english: “Would you two shut up for five minutes?”

lines.japanese:
「いいんだよ春希くん。
わたし、全然気にしてないんだから」
lines.english: “It’s all right, Haruki. I truly don’t mind.”

lines.japanese: 「け、けど雪菜…」
lines.english: “B-But, Setsuna…”

lines.japanese:
「わたしは、嫌じゃなかったから。
…みんなで旅行」
lines.english: “I didn’t dislike the idea. A trip with everyone, I mean.”

lines.japanese:
「春希くんは、嫌かな？
それとも、何か用事があった？」
lines.english: “Would you rather not go, Haruki? Or did you have other plans?”

lines.japanese: 「ない、けど…」
lines.english: “No, but…”

lines.japanese:
そうだ。
今までにもあった。
雪菜が、家族に嘘をついたこと。
lines.english: Right. This had happened before. Setsuna had lied to her family.

lines.japanese:
三年前、クリスマスに三人で温泉旅行に行ったとき。
三月前、真夜中の公園で喧嘩もできなかったとき。
lines.english: Three years ago, when the three of us took that Christmas trip to the hot springs. Three months ago, when we couldn’t even bring ourselves to fight in a park at midnight.

lines.japanese:
ああ…
結局いつも、俺のせいだ。
lines.english: Of course. In the end, it was always my fault.

lines.japanese:
今回の無理やりな旅行を雪菜が断らないのも、
もしかしたら…
lines.english: Perhaps the reason Setsuna hadn’t refused this absurd trip was also…

lines.japanese: 「…どうやら話はまとまったみたいだな？」
lines.english: “…Sounds as though that settles it.”

lines.japanese:
「楽しい旅にしようよ。
せっかく久々に四人揃ったんだからさ」
lines.english: “Let’s make it a good trip. It’s been so long since all four of us were together.”

lines.japanese: 「…ったく」
lines.english: “…Honestly.”

lines.japanese:
脳天気な犯罪者どもが、
後ろを振り返り、俺たち二人に笑いかける。
lines.english: The two cheerful criminals looked over their shoulders and smiled at us.

lines.japanese:
それはあまりに強引で、身勝手で、
こっちの心の隙をつくテロリストの笑顔だったけど。
lines.english: They were the smiles of terrorists—pushy, selfish, and aimed straight at the cracks in our resolve.

lines.japanese:
でも、そいつらの信奉する正義が何なのか
わかってしまっている俺たちは、
これ以上、責める言葉を持たない。
lines.english: But we knew the righteous cause they believed they were serving, so we had no words left to condemn them with.
“Oh…”
“Hm?”
“Snow…”

lines.japanese:
雪菜が見上げる先を目で追うと、
車窓の外に、白い粒が天から舞い降りていた。
lines.english: I followed Setsuna’s gaze and saw white flakes drifting down from the sky beyond the window.

lines.japanese:
高速を、ペーパードライバーの安全運転で三時間。
もう、東京は遙か遠くに過ぎ去り、
今は山梨か、そろそろ長野か…
lines.english: Three hours on the expressway at an inexperienced driver’s painfully cautious pace had carried us far beyond Tokyo. Perhaps we were in Yamanashi now, or nearing Nagano.

lines.japanese:
そんな『雪国』と呼ばれる地域に入ったんだろう。
いつの間にか、俺たちの周囲に降りてくる雪が、
見る見るうちに激しさを増していく。
lines.english: We must have entered one of those regions people called “snow country.” Around us, the snow was growing heavier by the minute.

lines.japanese: 「雪だね」
lines.english: “It’s snowing.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ…」
lines.english: “Yeah…”

lines.japanese:
『雪』や『うん』や『ああ』くらいしかない、
相変わらずたどたどしい会話。
lines.english: Our conversation remained as halting as ever, made up of little more than “snow,” “mm-hm,” and “yeah.”

lines.japanese:
けれど多分、今、俺たちは
百の言葉以上の情報を共有してると思う。
lines.english: Yet I thought we were sharing more in that moment than a hundred words could have said.

lines.japanese:
だって、車の中から雪降る空を見上げると、
どうしても、あの日のことを思い出してしまうから。
lines.english: Because looking up at falling snow from inside a car made it impossible not to remember that day.

lines.japanese:
三年前の光景を…
あの時の、三人きりの一泊旅行で見た空を。
lines.english: The scene from three years ago—the sky we had seen on that overnight trip, when there were only three of us.

lines.japanese: 「寒くない？」
lines.english: “Are you cold?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、平気」
lines.english: “No, I’m fine.”

lines.japanese: 「そう…」
lines.english: “I see…”

lines.japanese: 「うん…」
lines.english: “Mm-hm…”

lines.japanese:
肩が触れあうほどの近さにいながら、
お互い、自分からは触れられないもどかしさ。
lines.english: We sat close enough for our shoulders to touch, yet neither of us could bring ourselves to reach out first.

lines.japanese: 間違いなく、今、同じ記憶を見てるはずなのに…
lines.english: Even though we must have been reliving the same memory…

lines.japanese:
いや、見てるものが同じだからこそ、
二人の間にある見えない壁に阻まれてしまう。
lines.english: No—because we were reliving the same thing, the invisible wall between us held us apart.

lines.japanese: 「綺麗だね…」
lines.english: “It’s beautiful…”

lines.japanese:
「ちょっと大粒だけどな。
ベタ雪っぽいかも」
lines.english: “The flakes are a little big. Looks like wet snow.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ…そうかも」
lines.english: “Hehe… I suppose so.”

lines.japanese:
でも今は、こうして普通に話せるだけでいい。
俯かず、互いの顔を見て、軽く笑顔まで浮かべて…
lines.english: For now, it was enough that we could talk normally—that we could meet each other’s eyes instead of looking down, and even manage a faint smile.

lines.japanese:
「二人とも、今のうちに寝といた方がいいぞ。
向こうに着いたらすぐにゲレンデ直行だからな」
lines.english: “You two should sleep while you can. We’re going straight to the slopes when we arrive.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でも…」
lines.english: “But…”

lines.japanese: 「運転、代わらなくていいのか？」
lines.english: “Don’t you need someone to take over driving?”

lines.japanese:
「いいっていいって。
無理やり連れ出したのは武也なんだからさ。
ちゃんと責任取らせるよ」
lines.english: “He’ll be fine. Takeya dragged us out here, so he can take responsibility.”

lines.japanese: 「俺、お前だけは運転手に数えてたんだけど…」
lines.english: “You were the one person I was counting on as a second driver…”

lines.japanese:
ダッシュボードの時計は、
いつの間にか５時を過ぎていた。
lines.english: At some point, the dashboard clock had ticked past five.

lines.japanese:
「ほら、寒かったらこの毛布使いなよ。
一枚しかないけど、ないよりましでしょ」
lines.english: “Here. Use this if you’re cold. There’s only one blanket, but it’s better than nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「で、でも…」
lines.english: “B-But…”

lines.japanese:
と、申し訳なさそうに口ごもる雪菜は、
なぜかというか、やっぱりというか、
困ったように、すぐ隣の俺を見つめてくる。
lines.english: Setsuna faltered apologetically, then turned to me with a helpless look—for no reason, or for the most obvious reason in the world.

lines.japanese:
「皆の言う通りだ。
少しは寝た方がいいよ、雪菜」
lines.english: “They’re right. You should get some sleep, Setsuna.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese:
依緒が差し出した毛布を受け取ると、
両手で拡げて、雪菜を覆うように肩に掛ける。
lines.english: I took the blanket from Io, opened it in both hands, and draped it around Setsuna’s shoulders.

lines.japanese: 「起きたら、一面銀世界だ」
lines.english: “When you wake up, the whole world will be white.”

lines.japanese: 「春希くん…」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
その時、かすかにだけど、
今日、初めて雪菜の身体に触れた。
lines.english: And in that moment, ever so lightly, I touched Setsuna for the first time that day.

lines.japanese:
暗がりの中、
雪菜の瞳がずっと俺の横顔を見つめてる。
lines.english: In the darkness, her eyes remained fixed on my profile.

lines.japanese:
その視線を意識しないように、
毛布を雪菜の膝まで覆い、そして離れる。
lines.english: Trying not to acknowledge her gaze, I drew the blanket down over her knees and moved away.

lines.japanese:
そうして離れた後も、
雪菜はずっと、俺から視線を外そうとしなかった。
lines.english: Even after I withdrew, Setsuna never looked away from me.

lines.japanese:
咎めるような、気づかうような…
そんな光を灯したまま、ずっと。
lines.english: The light in her eyes seemed to accuse me and worry over me at once… and it never wavered.

lines.japanese: 「ん…んぅ…」
lines.english: “Mm… mmm…”

lines.japanese:
肩が触れあうほどの近さにいながら、
お互い、自分からは触れられないもどかしさ。
lines.english: We sat close enough for our shoulders to touch, yet neither of us could bring ourselves to reach out first.

lines.japanese: 「すぅ…すぅぅ…」
lines.english: “Hh… hhh…”

lines.japanese: …なんてものは、いつの間にか有名無実化していた。
lines.english: At some point, though, all that hesitation had quietly ceased to matter.

lines.japanese: 「…何だよ？」
lines.english: “…What?”

lines.japanese: 「別にぃ」
lines.english: “Nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「ねぇ」
lines.english: “Not a thing.”

lines.japanese: 「くっ…」
lines.english: “Damn it…”

lines.japanese: 眠ってしまった雪菜の頭が、俺の肩にもたれかかる。
lines.english: Setsuna’s sleeping head had come to rest against my shoulder.

lines.japanese:
でも俺は、その彼女の肩を抱き寄せることもできず、
ただ、彼女の支えになっているだけだった。
lines.english: But I could not put an arm around her. All I could do was remain still and support her weight.
“Mm…”

lines.japanese:
雪菜を覆ったはずの毛布は、
いつの間にか、俺と雪菜を一緒に包んでいる。
lines.english: Before I knew it, the blanket meant for Setsuna was covering us both.

lines.japanese:
雪菜が、そうしてしまった。
戸惑う俺に、まるで腹を立てたように、強引に。
lines.english: Setsuna had made it so, pulling it over me almost forcibly, as though angry at my hesitation.

lines.japanese:
だから、俺たちの距離は強制的にゼロになり、
その後しばらくして、雪菜の頭が俺の肩に触れ、
そしてゆっくり傾き、今の状態を作り上げた。
lines.english: She had closed the distance between us by force. A little later, her head found my shoulder, tilted slowly sideways—and left us like this.

lines.japanese: 雪菜の身体から、彼女の体温が伝わってくる。
lines.english: Setsuna’s body was warm against mine.

lines.japanese:
一枚の毛布で、二人が一度に、
それも一番温まれる最良の方法を取っただけ。
lines.english: We were only sharing a blanket in the warmest way two people could.

lines.japanese:
…なんて、そんな熱効率の話じゃないってことは、
この場の誰もがわかってる。
lines.english: But everyone in the car knew this had nothing to do with thermal efficiency.

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ、ん、んぅ…」
lines.english: “Mmm… nn…”

lines.japanese: 雪菜の重みが、俺に心地良い安らぎを与える。
lines.english: The weight of Setsuna against me was deeply comforting.

lines.japanese:
閉じた目から伸びる長い睫毛。
甘い寝息をこぼす濡れた唇。
誰が見ても認める、端正で、かつ可愛らしい顔。
lines.english: Long lashes against her closed eyes. Damp lips parting with each soft breath. A face anyone would have called both beautiful and adorable.

lines.japanese:
こんな彼女に枕の役目を仰せつかった男は、
誰もがその瞬間を至福の時と感じるに違いない。
lines.english: Any man lucky enough to be her pillow would have thought himself in heaven.

lines.japanese:
それは…俺だって。
いや、俺だからこそ、なおさら。
lines.english: I was no exception. If anything, I felt it more keenly than anyone.

lines.japanese: だって雪菜は…俺の大切な女性だから。
lines.english: Because Setsuna was… a woman very dear to me.

lines.japanese:
どれだけすれ違っても。
どれだけ互いが傷ついても。
lines.english: No matter how often we missed each other. No matter how deeply we hurt one another.

lines.japanese: たとえ、何度別れを告げられたとしても。
lines.english: No matter how many times she told me it was over.

lines.japanese:
車窓の外に降る雪は、
少しずつ、その密度を増していく。
lines.english: Outside the window, the falling snow grew steadily thicker.

lines.japanese:
冬は、まだ終わらない。
俺たちの『ＷＨＩＴＥ　ＡＬＢＵＭの季節』は続いてる。
lines.english: Winter was not over. Our season of “White Album” went on.
“Mm…”

lines.japanese:
雪菜の手のひらが、
俺の手に重ねられる。
lines.english: Setsuna’s palm comes softly down to rest over the back of my own hand.

lines.japanese:
そして今の俺には、
その手を離す気持ちも、
握り返す勇気も持てないでいた。
lines.english: And now, I have neither the will to pull away, nor the courage to close my hand around hers in return.

lines.japanese:
けれど、今は冬。
俺たちの時間は、必ずまた動き出す。
lines.english: But it is winter now. Our time will inevitably start moving again.

lines.japanese:
雪の降る日に俺たちは近づき、
雪の降る夜に俺たちは傷つき。
lines.english: On days when snow fell, we drew closer; on nights when snow fell, we hurt each other.

lines.japanese:
そして今日、雪の降る夜明けに…
俺たちは、どんな関係を築いていくんだろう。
lines.english: And today, at dawn after a snowy night… what kind of relationship would we build between us from here on out?
